findings.text: The bundled list `app/server/auth/common-passwords.txt` is a non-.js file under app/server. app/test/unit/import-boundaries.test.js `fileFindings` (lines 728-748) reports every file under server/, api/ or worker/ that is not .js («a file that is not .js: …»; the one exception is a vendored .d.ts twin), and IB-1 asserts the real tree has no finding, so IB-1 turns red; A21 says import-boundaries is unchanged. The design names the .txt in 5 places. Needed, as decisions/0137 «N2b, form of the list» now decides: the list is the module `app/server/auth/common-passwords.js` (a frozen set of strings generated once from the named source, source, commit and licence in its header comment), imported by password.js (no fs read); C20, §3, 4.9.2 (the file rules and the reading), §9.1 PW-4 (the header and entry rules read from the module), §12 B6 and §17 updated to it; the IB guard stays unchanged. Recorded as a finding only; ORCH says it is not a reason to fail the rest.

The rework locks the admin's users row as the first statement of every login, «so every admin attempt, from any address, is serialised», and holds it for the scrypt (about 0.5 s). The admin's users row carries no counter (he is never locked; the delay is per address in login_delays), so the lock protects nothing there, but it lets attackers from several addresses keep the row busy: each queued attempt waits under the 4 s request deadline, and the admin's own right password from a clean address waits behind them or answers 503. That works against REQ-114's description («the platform admin is never locked (an attacker who knows his e-mail must not keep him out of «Стоп всем»)») and the spirit of c5 («the right password from a second IP logs in at once»). Needed: no row lock on the admin's users row; the admin's per-address state is locked instead (`insert … on conflict do nothing` then `select … for update` of the login_delays row of that address); AUTH-RACE-3 keeps its expectation for one address, a new pg case shows that parallel wrong admin attempts from other addresses do not delay a right login from a clean address (200 within the deadline), and M52 is restated against that row.

The capacity note counts memory only (2 GB, about 12 areas of 128 MiB). A Vercel Hobby function has 1 vCPU (same page as F30): N parallel scrypt computations at N = 2^17 take about N × 0.5 s of CPU, so beyond about 7 parallel logins the 4 s deadline answers 503 to all of them. Name this in §7 and in the post-deploy record (measure one login's time on production).

MIT requires the copyright notice and the permission notice in every copy; the planned one-line header names the licence and the copyright only. Include the full MIT text in the header (or a licence file beside the list).

A third-party word list of thousands of lines enters a repository whose `npm run traces` scans every file; the developer runs traces on it before the commit and filters any entry that matches a trace word, so step 10 is not surprised.

Say in so many words that the deadline answer of item 3 is disarmed once COMMIT is sent (item 4), so a transaction that committed is never answered 503 by the race; the text implies it but a developer could keep both.
